clue.text: Second team invested in poxy finance

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: poxy is slang for worthless or rubbish, that is poor
in bridge North and South play as a partnership, so NS is a team

explanation.surface: A sneering remark about a second team being funded with shoddy money.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South are partners, so the pair counts as a team. 'Poxy' is British slang for shoddy or worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: To fund something, such as an event or a team, is to back it with money as a patron.

clue.text: Calm North Yorkshire town

definitions.meaning: to soothe or quieten someone down
a market town in the Yorkshire Dales, start of the Carlisle railway line

explanation.definitionFit: Settle means to calm down and is also a town in Ribblesdale, North Yorkshire.

clue.text: Forceful surge forward after end of ten hours being furious

indicators.note: being furious suggests the letters are thrown wildly into a new order
end of picks the final letter of the word ten

explanation.surface: After ten hours of waiting, an angry crowd surges forward.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the end of ten, is mixed with HOURS by 'being furious'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a sudden forceful rushing forward, as of water or a crowd.

clue.text: Is cat among horses up for the earth-shattering record?

indicators.note: among puts one piece in the middle of the other
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mares are female horses
moggy or mog is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat startles some horses, causing a recording of a huge disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' applies only to the horses, so SERAM comes from turning them round. MOG is British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A seismogram is the trace recorded by a seismograph during an earthquake.

clue.text: Don't tear off to see North Yorkshire town

indicators.note: don't tells us to reverse the sense of off, turning it into its opposite on

parts.note: to rip off is to tear off

explanation.surface: A warning not to rip something off, to see a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Not 'tear off' but its opposite: RIP plus ON. RIPON is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire, near Harrogate.

clue.text: Exercise in ring, ending in whack for the motivator

indicators.note: in places the exercise inside the ring of bells

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
PT is physical training, school exercise

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of the word whack

explanation.surface: A boxer training in the ring finishes with a punch, which gets the coach fired up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a boxing ring, but it means bells ringing; PT is the school abbreviation for physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: An encouraging speech is something that motivates a team or person before a challenge.

clue.text: Smoke that's brown rising in foreign food

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the dish

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom upwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A brown cigar's smoke drifting up over some exotic cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' as a noun can mean a cigar, not just the vapour; 'rising' turns TAN into NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin cigar, something one smokes.

clue.text: Advertise job

definitions.meaning: to put up a notice publicly

explanation.definitionFit: To post a notice is to advertise it, and a post is also a position at work.

clue.text: A poet like Byron forgetting name, like 21 and 23, say?

indicators.note: forgetting means a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: Byron was one of the English Romantic poets

explanation.surface: A Byronic poet who cannot remember a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 and 23 are SAGE and THYME, both fragrant herbs. 'forgetting' drops N from ROMANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbs such as these are fragrant, giving off a pleasant smell, the 'say' signalling examples.

clue.text: Token food before drink

parts.note: one's keep is one's food and board
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A voucher for a meal, followed by a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept as a memento, a token of remembrance.

clue.text: Prominence one observed on front of swimming trunks

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or prominence, common on Dartmoor

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of the word swimming

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone spots a bulge on the front of a pair of swimming trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming trunks' looks like one phrase, but 'trunks' alone is the definition, in its sense of human torsos; 'on' places I after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk is the human body without head or limbs, and the plural of torso here uses the Italian form.

clue.text: Part of the way open is to nearest South Yorkshire town

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters lying inside the following words

parts.words: the way open is to nearest

explanation.surface: Directions telling a driver which stretch of road is open to the nearest town.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'oPEN IS TO NEarest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Penistone is a market town in South Yorkshire, near Barnsley.

clue.text: Frantic having to survive, far from great

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure
minute means tiny, the opposite of great in size

explanation.surface: Panicking about surviving at all, let alone doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: MINUTE is the adjective pronounced my-NEWT, meaning very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at the final moment before a deadline is typically hurried and frantic.

clue.text: Inelegantly swan dips to cause bubbles to surface?

definitions.text: Inelegantly swan dips to cause bubbles to surface?

indicators.note: inelegantly says the letters of swan dips move about clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A swan ducking its head under the water, sending bubbles up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an ungainly swan dipping might produce bubbles from below by breaking wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking wind under water is exactly what would send bubbles rising to the surface.

clue.text: Fido's legs struggling to get round old part of London

indicators.note: to get round means to surround something, so the mixed letters enclose the other piece
struggling suggests the letters writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: An old dog on shaky legs struggles to get around a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges FIDOS LEGS, and 'to get round' puts that around O. The ISLE OF DOGS is a district in London's Docklands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is a former dockland peninsula in East London, home to Canary Wharf.

clue.text: North Yorkshire town laughs, bit of a slow burner

parts.note: giggles are little laughs
a wick is the part of a candle that burns slowly

explanation.surface: A town full of giggling and a gradually building comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: GIGGLESWICK is a village near Settle in North Yorkshire, known for its public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Giggleswick is a small settlement in the Craven district of North Yorkshire.

clue.text: Having to understand about oxygen chart is student of the earth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the rest

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a log is a record or chart, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: To understand oxygen, a chart is needed by a science student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' and 'is' look like padding in the surface, but 'is' supplies letters at the end of the inserted run.
explanation.definitionFit: A geologist studies the rocks and structure of the earth.

clue.text: Polish European not finishing up year in West Yorkshire town

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rub is to polish

indicators.note: not finishing drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: a Swede is a European from Sweden

explanation.surface: A Polish European worker who has not finished the year in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality beside 'European', but it is the verb RUB. 'not finishing' turns SWEDE into SWED, and 'up' turns RUBSWED into DEWSBUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewsbury is a minster town in the Kirklees district of West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Letter from Greece about tyrannical leader that's appreciated as evidence of suffering

indicators.note: about means going round, so the Greek letter wraps the other piece

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word tyrannical

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, said when something is appreciated

explanation.surface: A Greek letter about a tyrant that is welcomed as proof of hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you, the thing said when something is appreciated.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks resembling Christ's wounds, taken as signs of suffering.

clue.text: Conclude there's a requirement for an unexpected dinner guest to eat nothing

indicators.note: to eat means to take something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.words: a requirement for an unexpected dinner guest
parts.note: an extra plate must be laid when an unforeseen guest arrives for dinner
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A host notes that a surprise visitor needs a place at the table but is given nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts O inside EXTRA PLATE, between the P and the L.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to infer or deduce beyond known facts, which is to draw a conclusion.

clue.text: West Yorkshire town where pert rear seen through hay on top of you

indicators.note: seen through means one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: a bale is a bundle of hay

indicators.note: rear picks the final letter of the word pert

parts.note: Y is a common short form for you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A cheeky bottom glimpsed through a haystack in a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pert rear' looks like a body part, but 'rear' takes the last letter of 'pert'; 'seen through' puts it inside BALE, and Y goes under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Batley is a town in the Kirklees district of West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Didn't go steady after a wobble

indicators.note: after a wobble suggests the letters of steady are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remained, holding steady after a moment of unsteadiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained in place rather than leaving.

clue.text: Elder plant

definitions.meaning: a wise old person, a senior respected for wisdom
a grey-leaved herb used in stuffing

explanation.definitionFit: Sage means both a wise elder figure and the culinary herb Salvia.

clue.text: West Yorkshire town's ref not surprisingly in agreement

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for agreement

parts.note: a pact is an agreement or treaty

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that ref not turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A football referee who, unexpectedly, agrees with a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like it negates 'surprisingly', but it is anagram fodder: 'surprisingly' rearranges REF NOT into ONTEFR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontefract is a historic town in West Yorkshire, famous for liquorice cakes.

clue.text: Plant which has healing properties, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the answer sounds like the word that follows from the clue's description

parts.note: time is said to heal all wounds, as in time is a great healer

explanation.surface: A medicinal herb said to cure ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which has healing properties' looks like part of the definition of a herb, but it points to TIME, the great healer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb of the mint family.

clue.text: See 12
Heading off big fish, US supercarrier adjusts conclusion, being in accord

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter from the word for a big fish

parts.note: a tuna is a large ocean fish

indicators.note: adjusts conclusion changes the last letter of the warship's name

parts.note: the USS Nimitz is a famous American aircraft carrier

explanation.surface: A naval report about a big fish and an American carrier changing its final position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' turns TUNA into UNA; 'adjusts conclusion' swaps the final Z of NIMITZ for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimity is complete agreement among everyone, the state of all being of one mind.

clue.text: West Yorkshire town, disparate, lacking leadership

indicators.note: lacking leadership means losing the first letter of the word

parts.note: motley means varied or made of disparate elements

explanation.surface: A town of mixed people who have no one in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking leadership' drops the M from MOTLEY. OTLEY is a market town in Wharfedale.
explanation.definitionFit: Otley is a market town on the River Wharfe in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Still to come to grips with new road, finding way back

indicators.note: to come to grips with means to hold tight around something, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: yet means still, as in not yet done

indicators.note: new signals the letters of road are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A traveller still has to tackle a newly built road before heading back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way back' is the definition, not a direction: 'new' rearranges ROAD into ARDO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a very long time ago, the start of time, which is a long way back.

clue.text: Tried, perhaps, to fill middle of cheese dish

indicators.note: to fill means to go inside something, putting one piece within the other
middle of takes the central letters of the phrase cheese dish

parts.note: say means perhaps or for example

explanation.surface: Someone attempted, perhaps, to stuff the centre of a cheesy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the central four letters of the two words run together, not of each word separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, so essayed means attempted.
